facts.statement: Neanis fossils date to the Early Eocene epoch.
The genus Neanis was described by Shufeldt in 1913.
Neanis species are found in the Late Wasatchian stratum (51-52 million years ago) of the Early Eocene Green River Formation in the Western-Central USA.
facts.quote: Both are known from the Late Wasatchian (51-52 MYA) stratum of the Early Eocene Green River Formation of the Western-Central USA.

facts.statement: Neanis is an extinct genus of bird that is probably related to woodpeckers and toucans.
facts.quote: Neanis is an extinct genus of bird probably related to woodpeckers and toucans.

facts.statement: The family Primobucconidae, which originally included Neanis, has been moved to the order Coraciiformes.
facts.quote: Indeed, the only remaining genus of the family is Primobucco (without kistneri), and the family as such has been moved to the Coraciiformes.

facts.statement: Neanis schucherti appears to share traits with Hassiavis and might even be a cypselomorph.
facts.quote: Neanis schucherti appears to share some traits with Hassiavis and might even be a cypselomorph

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Neanis is Coracii.
